h1: The 5 Best Monochrome Laser Printers for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mono Laser Printers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: two true mono laser printers plus three close alternatives for home offices, compared on duplex, wireless, toner and price.
mainKeyword: monochrome laser printer for home office
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is our top pick: a true mono laser with duplex, wireless and separate drum and toner. The HP LaserJet M209d is the cheaper wired-only mono option. Two color lasers and one inkjet round out the list for offices that occasionally need more.
intro: The honest problem with this category is supply: only two printers in our pool are truly monochrome lasers. Search results blur mono lasers, color lasers and inkjets together, and buyers pay for color capability they never use or inkjet cartridges that dry out between jobs.

We reviewed five printers: two mono lasers, two color lasers that print black and white well, and one inkjet as a contrast. Ranking is based on the spec sheet: engine type, duplex, wireless, toner design and price tier. We say clearly where a pick is not a mono laser.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A true mono laser with wireless, duplex and separate drum and toner.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW prints black only with a laser engine, handles two-sided jobs, accepts wireless and phone printing, and keeps the drum and toner as separate parts. Brother tends to accept off-brand toner.

It beats the HP M209d because it adds wireless and a lower long-term running cost from the split drum design, though it costs more in the $200-500 bucket.

Best for regular document volume. The caveat is the higher upfront price.

products.name: HP LaserJet M209d Laser Printer, Black and White
products.verdict: A cheaper mono laser, wired only.
products.description:
The M209d is a black-and-white laser with automatic duplex, a plain USB cable link and a warm-up of roughly ten to fifteen seconds from cold. Firmware on HP machines can limit off-brand toner.

It ranks below the Brother because it lacks wireless, but it costs less in the $100-200 bucket.

Buy it for a desk with a printer cable nearby. The caveat is toner restrictions that can raise running costs.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: Not mono-only, but a good fit for mostly black-and-white offices that sometimes need color.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW does color as well as black, runs at about 19 pages a minute, holds 250 sheets and prints on both sides. Brother tends to accept off-brand toner.

It ranks under the mono lasers because it does more than this guide's title asks, and color toner adds cost. It is the pick if you sometimes need color.

Good for mixed documents. The caveat is the extra consumables.
products.idealFor: Mostly B&W offices needing occasional color.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Wireless Duplex Laser Printer
products.verdict: A fast all-in-one color laser with an auto document feeder.
products.description:
The Canon MF753Cdw II is a color laser multifunction that feeds stacks through a document feeder, prints about 35 pages a minute, keeps the drum apart from the toner and does two-sided printing over Wi-Fi. Off-brand toner support is hit and miss.

It ranks below the Brother color laser on price tier and toner flexibility, but it prints nearly twice as fast.

Buy it for busier offices that scan stacks. The caveat is that it is not a budget machine.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 9135 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: An inkjet for offices that want a feeder and fax, not laser economics.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 9135 uses ink rather than toner, and adds a document feeder, two-sided printing and scanning, and a short Instant Ink trial.

It ranks last as it misses the guide's mono laser brief, but it shows the alternative: easier color and fax, with ink that can dry out if unused.

Choose it if features matter over per-page cost. The caveat is that inkjet economics differ from laser.
products.idealFor: Offices that value features over laser economics.

whatMatters.detail: Mono lasers use a single black toner and cost less to run. Color lasers add three more toners. If you rarely print color, a mono laser wastes nothing.
A separate drum lets you replace only toner most of the time. This lowers cost per page. Check the listing for a split design.
Some firmware blocks off-brand toner. That raises running costs. Look for notes on third-party tolerance.
Automatic two-sided printing halves paper use. Manual duplex is slower. Check for automatic duplex.
Wireless lets phones and laptops print without cables. USB-only models need a nearby computer. Check connectivity in the title.

faq.q: Why are only two printers true mono lasers?
faq.a: Our pool contained only two. The rest are color lasers or inkjets that appear in related searches, and we label them clearly.
Buying a color laser they use only for black text, then paying for four toners.

faq.q: Is a mono laser worth over an inkjet?
faq.a: For text-heavy offices, yes. Toner lasts and does not dry out.

faq.q: How do I set up wireless?
faq.a: Use the printer's panel or app to join your Wi-Fi, then add it on your device.

faq.q: How do I maintain a laser?
faq.a: Replace toner when prompted, and the drum when quality fades. Keep paper dry.
Brother is generally tolerant. HP firmware may block it, so check before buying.

finalTake: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best monochrome laser here for steady home office use. The HP M209d is the cheaper wired option, while the Brother and Canon color lasers suit those who need occasional color. The OfficeJet is for feature seekers.
